Container.Name: controlarr
Container.Overview: Stops, starts and restarts your other containers at set times of day, using the 24-hour clock. When several start together they go one at a time in your chosen order, with a wait after each, so they don't all hit the CPU, RAM and disks at once. Set schedules on the web page (light and dark modes) or with container labels. Needs the Docker socket so it can stop and start containers. Free forever: no paid tiers, no Pro account, no subscriptions.
Container.Changes: ### 0.2.0 (2026-11-10) - Catches up after a reboot: containers with both a stop and a start time are put back into the state their schedule says. - Pause a schedule, or skip just its next time, from the web page. - Recent activity on the web page, and optional alerts to Discord or ntfy. - Stops now go in reverse load order. - Fixed load order 0 being ignored, and times running twice when the clocks go back. - Container healthcheck.

Config.Name: Web page port
Config.Description: Port for the Controlarr web page.

Config.Name: Config folder
Config.Description: Where schedules.yml is kept. Schedules you set on the web page are saved here.

Config.Name: Docker socket
Config.Description: Lets Controlarr stop and start your containers. Don't change this.

Config.Name: Web page password
Config.Description: Optional. Anyone who can open the page can stop and start your containers, so set one if others are on your network. Any username works.

Config.Name: Alert URL
Config.Description: Optional. A Discord webhook or an ntfy topic URL (for example https://ntfy.sh/my-controlarr). You get a message when a container fails to stop or start.

Config.Name: Default wait after start (seconds)
Config.Description: Wait after starting an app Controlarr doesn't recognise, before starting the next one.

Config.Name: Longest healthcheck wait (seconds)
Config.Description: For containers with a healthcheck, the longest to wait for them to become healthy.

Config.Name: Catch up on start
Config.Description: true = when Controlarr starts (for example after a reboot), stop or start containers that have both a stop and a start time so they match their schedule.

Config.Name: Dry run
Config.Description: true = only log what would happen, don't stop or start anything.
